The search will be limited to Canadian parks and protected area organizations, with a focus on national, provincial, and territorial parks (Context). Sources will not be required to focus on disability and accessibility, provided they contain employment-related content. Both peer-reviewed literature and grey literature will be searched and reviewed. Methods: Peer-reviewed literature will include a search of the following collections: EBSCO (EconLit, Business Source Premier), ProQuest (ASSIA, PAIS Index, Policy File Index, Worldwide Political Science Abstracts, IBSS), and Web of Science (Core Collection: SSCI, SCI-Expanded, ESCI, AHCI, CPCI-SSH, CPCI-S, BKCI-SSH). Grey literature will be systematically searched through official websites of Canadian national, provincial and territorial park agencies in Canada, with targeted searches for employment and human resource policies and reports. Searches will not be restricted by date but will be limited to English-language sources. The targeted search will take place in September 2026. All identified sources will be imported into Covidence and screened in two stages (title/abstract and full text) against the inclusion criteria. Data will be extracted to capture document characteristics and accessibility or disability inclusion-related content. Findings will be reported using frequency counts and narrative descriptions to map key concepts, evidence types, and gaps. Any deviations from standard JBI scoping review methodology will be documented and justified.

articles.title: Rethinking Revictimization
articles.abstract: Survivors of childhood abuse have a heightened risk of experiencing adulthood interpersonal violence. Existing theories explain revictimization through the victim’s deficits and past experiences of violence. These theories fail to explain the causes of revictimization, can lead to ineffective interventions, and can harm victims. This article presents a secondary analysis of the qualitative literature inspired by Eve Tuck’s formulation of desire-based research, which originally aimed to address similar narratives in the fields of education research and Indigenous studies. This analysis shows the benefits of a theoretical approach that situates the individual’s motivations within an interpersonal, social, and cultural context.

articles.title: Revisiting Social Media’s Emotion-Engagement Affinity: Audiovisual Evidence from Political Communication on TikTok
articles.abstract: Despite considerable research on the use of emotion in online political communication, prior studies have largely relied on textual data. By focusing on TikTok, a highly audiovisual platform, this letter revisits the classic emotion-engagement affinity of social media by incorporating visual and audio components. Drawing on a large dataset of TikTok posts by politicians and parties in eight Western democracies, I test how multimodal emotional content associates with user engagement across different political ideologies. Results show that negative and high-arousal posts are associated with higher engagement across emotional forms. Although extremist and populist actors upload negative content more frequently, mainstream actors benefit just as much from an emotional communicative strategy.

articles.title: Is a Fourth Contingency Necessary in Social Theory? A Constructive Critique
articles.abstract: Contingency is a paradigm that opposes determinism, yet itself proves limited in its ability to explain the macro level. This article analyzes the epistemological foundation of both contingency and deterministic grand theories and establishes that both reduce objective reality in a manner that renders them possible, yet contradictory. A heuristic approach to reduction is proposed, deriving a solution to overcome it through a deductively argued necessity for a fourth contingency – one that manifests only in free and open deliberation concerning the true, the beautiful, the meaningful, and the useful. The fourth contingency is necessary where social change is carried out, but it is ignored in the reproduction of social models, where contingent rearrangements concern the redistribution of tensions and of the price. The latter is an inadequate solution: it does not remove social tensions but raises the production cost of social life.

articles.title: The Efficacy of Commercial Computer Games as Vocabulary Learning Tools for EFL Students: An Empirical Investigation
articles.abstract: The goal of the present study is to investigate how a commercial computer game (CCG) affects the productive and receptive vocabulary knowledge of EFL learners when they are not in a formal educational setting. More specifically, we investigated how CCGs assist learners in recognizing and producing English vocabulary over time (i.e., whether they only recognize the words when directly confronted with them or use them spontaneously). The investigation took place in an EFL context, and a sample of convenience of male students from a classroom at a private language institution was selected by the researchers. According to the results of statistical analyses, players' receptive and productive vocabulary knowledge significantly increased after playing the game. Additionally, it was evident that the learned words were retained to a high degree.

articles.title: Heterogeneous Effects of Local Government Financing Channels on Industrial Structure: Evidence from Provincial-Level Panel Data in China
articles.authors: Liangkun Shi, Huanqi Wu, Hanfei Yang
articles.abstract: Local government financing channels provide an essential perspective for understanding the investment decisions of local governments and their economic effects. In China, broadly defined local government debt includes two categories: statutory debt and the debt incurred by local government financial vehicles (LGFVs). This paper uses provincial-level panel data from 2016 to 2025, constructs a data-driven industrial structure index, and estimates a two-way fixed-effects model controlling for the overall debt scale. The empirical evidence suggests that the different financial channels on industrial structure are associated with different and opposing changes in industrial structure. When the debt composition shifts toward LGFV debts, the share of relatively high-productivity efficiency industries increases, particularly that of the tertiary sector. In contrast, when the debt composition shifts toward statutory debt, the share of relatively low-production efficiency industries increases, particularly that of the secondary sector. Therefore, the composition of local government debt, rather than its scale alone, is relevant to changes in regional industrial structure.

articles.title: V-FIRST: A Formal Syntax for Intelligence Requirements Construction (Vance Formula for Intelligence Requirements Syntax and Testing)
articles.abstract: Writing a priority intelligence requirement appears simple. Getting it right is not. One poorly built sentence at the start of the intelligence process can waste collection and leave decision-makers without usable answers. Doctrine defines requirements and places them in planning processes yet offers no method for constructing them. A review of public sources finds no published syntactic standard. V-FIRST v1.0 fills that gap. Named for its place at the start of both the intelligence process (Planning and Direction) and the collection management process, it sets fixed sentence forms for each level, component formulas, provenance keys, and a verb taxonomy tied to standards of proof. It answers a need first noted in a 1960 Studies in Intelligence call for “an adequate theory of requirements.” Released openly, V-FIRST is available for instruction, testing, adoption, and refinement.

articles.title: What counts as equitable? Incidence, spatial allocation and accessibility outcomes of a supply-side transit subsidy
articles.authors: Gregorio Luz, Janaina Carla de Carvalho Duarte, Walysson Tangrins Martins

subjects.name: Public Affairs, Public Policy and Public Administration

articles.abstract: Whether a public transport subsidy benefits the poor is usually settled by who is allocated more per trip. That angle shows only part of the picture. We put four questions to one instrument, combining operator expenditure, smartcard validations and vehicle GPS for the bus system of Belo Horizonte, Brazil, subsidized since 2022. First, who receives it, in monetary terms as the literature does, at finer resolution, costing each vehicle segment and dividing it among those aboard. Among riders the transfer is progressive, against prior Global South evidence, the poorest quintile receiving 1.68 times the richest. Second, how the fare distributes costs. That quintile also pays most, on incomes 8.7 times smaller, and 45.8% of riders pay more in fares than they cost. Third, where the money accumulates in the city. It is progressive by income, per rider and per place, because those most expensive to carry live in the poor bus-dependent periphery, yet regressive where disadvantage is accessibility, because an untargeted per-vehicle-kilometer payment follows demand, and enough riders there outweigh their lower cost each. Fourth, whether the access it buys is equitable, against four normative lenses across wide ranges of cumulative and gravity-based specifications. Utilitarian and sufficientarian verdicts hold almost throughout. Egalitarian and Rawlsian verdicts depend on the indicator, its parameter, and whether gains are absolute or relative. The equity of a supply-side subsidy is not one question with one answer. Answering one and stopping is not wrong but partial, and partiality is indistinguishable from selection unless alternatives are reported.

articles.title: Is 'Realism' the Best Way to Explain International Relations?
articles.abstract: Evaluating whether realism constitutes the premier theoretical framework for explaining international relations requires strict adherence to clear epistemological benchmarks: explanatory range, parsimony, and Lakatosian progressiveness. This essay argues that structural realism remains the superior general theory of global politics. By anchoring its explanatory architecture within a stable, parsimonious core defined strictly by systemic anarchy and the distribution of capabilities, realism accounts for the widest variety of macro-phenomena (including polarity, balancing dynamics, and security dilemmas) without sacrificing its structural utility. While prominent rival frameworks such as liberalism, neoliberal institutionalism, and constructivism provide descriptive richness for localised interactions, they systematically trade breadth for depth by introducing redundant causal variables. Through a sophisticated Lakatosian methodology, this paper demonstrates how realism utilizes its positive heuristic to absorb empirical anomalies into a protective belt of auxiliary hypotheses, successfully preserving its core structural baseline while generating independently verified theoretical progress.

articles.title: Wasted Bonus? The Urgent Case of Rebuilding the Education-Labor Alignment in Indonesia
articles.abstract: Indonesia's demographic bonus is usually described as peaking around 2030 and closing in 2045. Projections from the 2020 Population Census indicate the opposite: the age structure was most favourable in 2020, and has worsened in every projected year since, crossing 50 dependents per 100 working-age people in the early 2040s. Its composition is changing too: by 2050, nearly half of dependents will be people over 65, not children who later enter the workforce. The cohorts that decide the outcome are already in school. This scoping review maps what is known about the fit between Indonesia's education system and its labour market from 2013 to 2025, and locates where the evidence stops. Reported under PRISMA-ScR, searches covered OpenAlex, Crossref, ERIC, DOAJ, Garuda and SINTA alongside government sources in English and Indonesian. Of 762 records screened, 259 were included, charted to a common template and synthesised thematically. Co-occurrence of curriculum and labour-market concepts was mapped across a 640-record bibliographic corpus. Of the 259 included studies, 169 appeared from 2023 onward. Reported graduate deficits are consistently interpersonal, adaptive and digital rather than technical, with employers, students and researchers converging independently. Unmet employer demand concentrates in green, blue, digital and entrepreneurial work, the areas where training and measurement are weakest. More than 70% of vocational teachers in practical subjects lack the digital competence their curriculum assumes. Curriculum and labour concepts co-occur at 0.56 times the rate chance predicts, while each literature is internally dense at 1.58 and 2.61; Kurikulum Merdeka appears alongside employability, unemployment, skill mismatch or work readiness in no study. The two literatures do not run in parallel; they avoid one another. Indonesia is changing what it teaches faster than it measures what those changes do to employment, with less time to correct course than standard accounts of the demographic bonus imply.

articles.title: The Media Career of Artificial Intelligence in Europe’s Elite Press, 2015–2026
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a fixture of the news agenda, yet little comparative research traces its coverage across countries and across the generative turn marked by ChatGPT's release in late 2022. This study analyzes 43,986 articles from leading center-left and center-right newspapers in ten European countries and seven languages from 2015 to mid-2026. The articles were coded by an ensemble of large language models and the resulting classifications were validated against human judgment. Coverage grew, first peaking in the late 2010s and then surging far more dramatically after the release of ChatGPT, reaching more than seven times its earlier average level by the first half of 2026. AI coverage became markedly more negative, as net valence fell from +12.5 in 2022 to -21.7 in the first half of 2026. The decline occurred in all ten countries and among both center-left and center-right newspapers, without a consistent ideological pattern across countries. What made AI newsworthy also changed. Science and research fell from 26 to 12 per cent of coverage, while stories about disputes over copyright, jobs, and chatbot harms became more prominent. In its media career, AI thus shifted from an emerging technology covered largely through capabilities and potential applications toward a technology in use, increasingly covered through its consequences, conflicts, and governance.

articles.title: Women and AI: A Large-Scale, Validated Mapping of Women’s Under-Represented and Under-Recognized Contributions to AI Research
articles.abstract: Participation in AI research shapes which type of AI is built, whose societal needs it addresses, and how it is used in society. Despite increasing attention to gender diversity in AI, we lacksystematic evidence on the research topics, methods used, and collaboration structures associated with female AI researchers. This paper addresses this significant gap by developing the first large-scale, validated mapping of women’s contributions to both generative and non-generative AI research across data science and the main social science disciplines (economics, political science, and sociology). Using a sample of over 500,000 papers published between 2023 and 2026, we document three key findings. First, women are under-represented among academic AI authors across all four disciplines and recent years, and least represented in data science. Second, conditional on participating, women’s AI research is thematically distinctive: it is more applied, social and purpose-driven, concentrated in health, education and fairness, and, in data science, oriented towards using rather than building AI. Third, this distinctive work is heard less: conditional on working on the same AI topic women and men are cited equally, but the topics women disproportionately work on are themselves cited less, so women’s ideas receive systematically fewer citations. This voice gap is therefore a topic-composition penalty rather than a same-topic penalty, and it reduces efficiency by giving a distinctive, society-oriented research agenda too little voice in how AI develops.

articles.title: The Politics of Right and Wrong: Moral Appeals in Political Communication over Six Decades in Ten Western Democracies
articles.abstract: When politics is seen in a moral light, it fundamentally changes the terms of the game: Moralization both mobilizes and polarizes, testifying to its potency as a political force. Yet, despite the wealth of evidence on the consequences of moralization, we still have limited insight into politicians’ rhetorical use of moral appeals. This article empirically grounds existing theories by answering unresolved questions concerning the temporal, ideological, and topical variation in moral appeals cross-nationally. To do so, we develop a novel multilingual transformer model and analyse a large corpus of political text from ten Western democracies over six decades. We show, first, that political communication has become increasingly moralized over the past sixty years; second, that the tendency to moralize does not follow a consistent ideological pattern; and third, that presumably ‘moral’ and ‘non-moral’ topics can be equally framed in moral terms. Together, these findings qualify our understanding of political moralization: Rather than a fixed and stable property of political communication, moral appeals are used by politicians as a dynamic rhetorical tool.

articles.title: The Magica Inversion: When Protectors Discover Their Role in Producing the Harm They Sought to Prevent
articles.abstract: This paper introduces the Magica Inversion, a conceptual model explaining what occurs when actors who understand themselves as protectors discover that their own practices may also participate in producing the harm they seek to prevent. The concept takes its name from the categorical reversal in Puella Magi Madoka Magica, in which two apparently opposed categories are revealed to belong to the same generative structure; the paper uses this narrative structure as a cultural metaphor rather than translating the fictional transformation directly into a psychological model. The model begins with the Protective Self-Narrative, through which managers, teachers, caregivers, or other responsible actors interpret strict guidance, control, or correction as expressions of care, duty, or protection. Such intentions may be genuine, yet the social outcomes of these practices may diverge from their intended purposes, producing silence, reduced psychological safety, imitation of aggressive behavior, dependence, or withdrawal. The paper distinguishes Known Imperfection from Unknown Structural Meaning: an actor may already know that they are quick-tempered, perfectionistic, or controlling without recognizing how these traits function within a wider causal structure. Structural Feedback makes this hidden relationship visible by connecting dispersed events into a common generative pattern. When the actor then includes their own behavior as a variable in the causal model, a process termed Causal Self-Inclusion, the original protector identity may be reinterpreted. The Magica Inversion refers to this reversal of self-understanding: the discovery that a person who stood against a problem may also have participated in its production. The model does not describe a moral transformation from “good” to “bad,” nor does it assume that protective intention and harmful consequence are mutually exclusive. Instead, both may coexist within the same practice. Four post-inversion pathways are proposed: Narrative Repair, Narrative Rejection, Narrative Avoidance, and Defensive Retaliation. A longitudinal observational case is used to illustrate how Structural Feedback may be followed first by apparent acceptance and later by relational and informational avoidance, while avoiding claims about unobserved internal states. Finally, the paper proposes Identity-Preserving Correction as a repair principle that preserves legitimate protective purposes while revising harmful methods. The broader argument is that the deepest challenge of Structural Feedback is not discovering an unknown flaw, but discovering a new causal meaning in a flaw already known.

articles.title: Mahseer Breeding and Stocking: Insights from Studies on Scientific Literature, Newspapers and Social Media
articles.authors: Mahendra Singh Rawat, Ayana Krishnan, Prantik Das, VV Binoy
articles.abstract: Captive breeding and replenishing wild populations with hatchery reared individuals is a strategy utilised by many nations to conserve the iconic freshwater fishes mahseers, popularly known as the ‘tiger of the river’. We explored the research publications available on multiple academic databases, English newspapers published from their distribution range, and the videos and images posted on the social media platforms (YouTube, Facebook, X and Instagram) and the public engagement they received to get insights on the trends of breeding and stocking of all the known mahseer species. Our results revealed that scientific publications and newspaper articles on the breeding and stocking of these fishes were sparse, and the available ones came out mainly from a single nation, India, and focused on one species, T. putitora. Very few cross-national collaborations between the researchers working on these topics, and the absence of scientific analysis of post-release survival and growth of the juveniles of any mahseers raises concerns. Akin to other two streams of data studied, social media posts focusing on breeding and stocking of mahseers were also limited. The importance of sensitising the scientific community to extend the scope of mahseer breeding beyond a few popular species and developing effective post-release monitoring strategies, and translating positive sentiment and emotions of the public towards these activities, as evident in social media engagement, into broader support for the conservation of these fishes of ecological, economic and cultural importance are discussed.

articles.title: Colorism and the Moroccan COMPLEX(ION), Qahwi/Qahwia: Gender, Class, and the Rise of a Moroccan Social Media Slur
articles.abstract: The research about Colorism as a system of prejudice has been thorough and extensive, especially in Western academia. However, Moroccan scholarship’s focuses on the history of colorism, and since it is a culturally sensitive subject it often overlooks the forthcoming intricacies. The paper aims to examine colorism as a system of social stratification which intersects with Misogyny and Misandry in the digital environment. Furthermore, this paper primarily analyzes social media content which introduces a relatively “new” and under scrutinized term “Qahwi/Qahwia”, along with interview findings that explore how the term operates. The theoretical framework consists of postcolonial theory—namely Fanon’s Epidermalization of Inferiority, and Kimberle Crenshaw’s Intersectionality and lastly, John Suler’s Online Disinhibition Effect; each respectively investigating Morocco’s history and anthropology, race and gender, as well as the role of social media in prolonging discrimination by using seemingly “trivial” language.

articles.title: Light Before the Fall: Preventive Recognition and the Formation of Defensive Self-Narratives
articles.abstract: This paper develops a theoretical model explaining why recognition in the workplace does not always produce the same psychological or interpersonal outcomes. Building on the Dignity Lighter Model, which proposed authentic specific affirmation as a countermeasure to repeated micro-devaluation, the paper shifts attention from the giver of recognition to the recipient’s pre-existing self-narrative. It introduces Narrative Backbone as the relatively enduring but revisable structure through which individuals connect past experiences, current roles, relationships, abilities, values, symbolic identities, and imagined futures into an account of who they are. The paper further proposes Preventive Recognition as non-comparative recognition delivered before status threat, chronic devaluation, and defensive comparison become embedded in that narrative structure. To explain divergent outcomes, the paper presents the Recognition Bifurcation Model (RBM). According to the model, recognition may lead to preventive stabilization, but it may also be transformed into defensive vindication, comparative self-restoration, or defensive narrative preservation when it is filtered through rigid, threatened, or comparison-dependent self-stories. In contrast, when individuals can draw on multiple identity resources and reinterpret their past, recognition may support Constructive Narrative Reconstruction. This process is conceptualized as Self-Relighting: the rebuilding of self-worth and agency by reorganizing one’s own accumulated experiences into a new self-narrative rather than relying indefinitely on external affirmation. The central argument is that a psychologically strong self-story is not one that never breaks, but one that can be revised without reducing the whole self to a single failure, role, evaluation, or comparison. The paper therefore reframes workplace recognition as a path-dependent and narratively mediated process, with implications for dignity, identity threat, social comparison, leadership, and the prevention of defensive aggression.

articles.title: Influential Habitual Social Media Practices of Digital Technology (Social Media) Prompting the Concept of Fear of Missing Out (FoMO) among Youngsters
articles.authors: Dr. Abdullah Alfazeena, Dr. Manikkam K
articles.abstract: The booming social media habitat has tremendously influenced users of all ages by altering their ideas, thoughts, and behaviours toward themselves and others (Ibrahim et al., 2021). Continuous occurrence of such influential practices leads social media users to equip the Fear of Missing Out (FoMO). This concept deals with the ‘fear of losing something’ because of their decreased involvement. FoMO has psychologically impacted social media users to experience a sense of “... irritability, anxiety, and inadequacy”, while they restrain themselves from their habitual social media practices (Wortham, 2011). Similarly, the theory of practice suggested by Pierre Bourdieu (1994) illustrates the habitual imposition of certain cultures, which has adverse effects on humans' everyday practices. Social media usage has transformed into social media culture, insisting that the ‘power field’ be explored through anthropological practices. This research study aims to explore the social media practices among young adolescents, who equip FoMO with continuous involvement. Study utilises Qualitative In-Depth Interviews conducted among ten youngsters. Pierre Bourdieu’s Theory of Practice is underpinned within this study to develop an efficient theoretical and conceptual framework.

articles.title: Continuity, Rhythm, and Montage: Editing Techniques in Kaakha Kaakha (2003)
articles.abstract: This essay will also discuss how the editing process is used as a key cinematic element to construct narrative, emotion, and genre enhancement in the Tamil film, Kaakha Kaakha (2003), which was directed by Gautham Vasudev Menon. Based on a multi-theoretical framework comprising of continuity editing, the Soviet montage theory, rhythmic editing, neoformalist narrative theory, and the affective film theory the study examines how editing functions as both a constructive and expressive means. The important sequences are analyzed, including action encounters, romantic scenes, and scenes of individual loss, using a qualitative, scene-by-scene analytical approach to determine the editing patterns and their use in narrating the story. The results have shown that continuity editing is the structural backbone of the movie which makes the film spatially and temporally coherent by using shot-reverse-shot, eyeline match, and match-on-action techniques. Rhythmic editing is also very essential in adjusting the emotional level, as quick cuts increase the tension during a action shot and slower cut promotes intimacy during a romantic shot. In training and conflict sequences, Compression of time, dramatic effect, and creation of meaning: Montage is used to create meaning by juxtaposition of visual effects, especially through visual opposites. Moreover, the paper also indicates the overall effects of the editing strategies in the creation of the hybrid cinematic approach, which incorporates the classical Hollywood conventions and expressive montage approaches. Such hybridity does not only increase the engagement of the audiences but also supports the genres norms and leaves the tonal changes between the action, romance and melodrama. Finally, the paper highlights the importance of editing as a multidimensional process that defines the formal and affective aspects of the Tamil cinema.

articles.title: The Unequal Toll of Loneliness on Electoral Participation: Longitudinal Evidence from The Netherlands
articles.authors: Francesco Marolla, Arturo Bertero, Cristiano Vezzoni
articles.abstract: While declining turnout is often attributed to a lack of social integration, the political relevance of subjective disconnection has only recently drawn scholarly attention. Using eleven waves of the LISS panel in the Netherlands, we study how social and emotional loneliness relate to electoral participation, net of objective social position and objective social integration. Lower self-reported voting propensity is tied specifically to social loneliness, the perceived lack of a broader community network, whereas emotional loneliness shows no independent association once the social facet is accounted for. Separating stable between-person differences from within-person change, we find this gap concentrated among citizens who are chronically high in social loneliness, while within-person fluctuations show no association, indicating that the relationship is dispositional rather than situational and consistent with a link between chronic loneliness and weaker voting habits. Crucially, the gap is substantially narrower among citizens with greater education, political interest, and partisanship. The participatory cost of loneliness is therefore unevenly distributed across the electorate, falling hardest on citizens with the fewest civic resources.

articles.title: Lessons from History: Historical WaSH Programmes and the Decline of Summer Diarrhoeal Mortality
articles.abstract: Using high-frequency historical data on mortality (weekly) and temperature (daily), we examine the puzzle of the late decline of infant diarrhoeal mortality in British and Irish cities. While mortality from other faecal–oral diseases began falling before the 1880s alongside investments in urban water supply and waste disposal, large summer epidemics of infant diarrhoea persisted until the 1910s. We analyse a large panel of towns spanning the period 1893–1930 to characterise the temperature-infant mortality nexus and to identify turning points in this relationship. Two-way fixed effects models reveal the roles of flush toilet provision, reductions in fly populations, and infant feeding practices in the decline of infant diarrhoeal mortality. Our findings indicate that preventing lethal summer epidemics among young children required coordinated improvements in both domestic and environmental hygiene. We suggest that these findings provide historical support for contemporary calls for ‘transformative WaSH’ programmes.

articles.title: The Influencer I’ll Vote For: Mapping Politicians and Parties on TikTok
articles.abstract: TikTok, and social media generally, continue to rise as important spheres of political communication and information. Mapping how political elites use these platforms thus remains consequential to our understanding of the political arena. However, due to its relative infancy, we have yet to thoroughly study these patterns on TikTok across countries. In response to this shortcoming, this paper introduces Mapping Politicians and Parties on TikTok (MPPTikTok), a dataset of TikTok accounts for national MPs and parties across 17 Western democracies, comprising over 2,190 usernames. Using these to collect ≈260,000 posts, I then describe the supply of content (presence and posting activity) and the engagement it receives across party families. Both radical party families are proportionally more present, post more, and receive more engagement than the Mainstream. The Radical Left leads most clearly in proportional presence and posting activity, while achieving engagement levels comparable to the Radical Right, with differences between them depending on the metric.

articles.title: Calibrating Synthetic Respondents: A Within-Persona Experiment on Public Reactions to Protest in Turkey
articles.authors: MEHMET FUAT KINA, Helin Yaren Ekmen
articles.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to simulate survey respondents, yet the inference pipeline that turns a persona into a response is rarely calibrated for the population and outcome it is applied to. This study makes population- and outcome-specific calibration the research task itself. Using a nationally representative survey in Turkey as the benchmark, we construct persona-conditioned synthetic respondents for all 2,615 survey participants and search a structured space of persona content, sampling strategies, temperatures, model backbones, and prompt framings. Calibration is assessed against two held-out outcomes that carry the response structures on which social movement research typically rests, a rare binary measure of protest participation and a five-point attitude item, and the selected protocols differ between the two. We then run a within-persona synthetic experiment that places the same protest for Kurdish-language education in a political opportunity and a political threat context. The threat context lowers simulated movement legitimacy and willingness to attend, and the simulated contrasts differentiate by political orientation, ethnicity, and education in the directions theory anticipates. Calibration is a precondition for reading synthetic experiments, not a robustness check appended to them.

articles.title: The Politics of Threat Construction: Securitisation as a Site of Contestation in Georgia’s Public Sphere
articles.authors: Mariam Bibilashvili, Zinaida Bechná, Kornely Kakachia
articles.abstract: Moving beyond studies on contemporary security challenges posed by information manipulation, economic coercion, and military pressure, this article problematises the securitisation of foreign interference narratives by political leaders through the case of Georgia (2023–2025). The analysis draws on 325 social media posts by high-level officials and ten in-depth interviews with civic actors resisting state narratives. It relies on securitisation theory to (1) examine how political elites frame domestic actors as instruments of the Western interference despite the country’s constitutionally anchored pro-European orientation and overwhelming public support for EU integration, and (2) explore how counter-securitisation unfolds among civic actors. The findings reveal a structured securitising narrative grounded in sovereigntist logic, invoking historical memory, identity threats, and conspiracy framings to delegitimise civic actors as rootless and foreign aligned. However, rather than generating stable audience acceptance this securitising move triggers counter-securitisation as civic actors contest the proposed threat hierarchy, reframe Russia and democratic backsliding as primary dangers, and additionally mobilise performative resistance through street protest. The analysis highlights the agency of civic actors who simultaneously occupy the positions of securitised subjects and a segment of the audience and complements post-structuralist understandings of the securitisation as a co-constitutive and iterative rather than a linear process.

articles.title: Distributed Citizenship in Local-Oriented Online Communities: A Behavioral Repertoire of Civic Roles Across 50 North American City Groups

subjects.name: Public Affairs, Public Policy and Public Administration

articles.abstract: Local-oriented online communities increasingly serve as informal spaces where residents exchange local knowledge, discuss public issues, and encounter local news. Yet existing research often treats these communities as digital third spaces, with less attention to how civic labor is distributed among participants. This study understands these communities as components of local information infrastructures, examining how civic roles are distributed by analyzing year-long data from 50 highly active North American city subreddits in 2024. Focusing on 43,263 sustained users, we combine media-domain matching, LLM-assisted topic classification, latent profile analysis, and qualitative case comparison. The analysis identifies six behavioral civic roles: National News Commentators, Platform-Native Political Discussants, Local Civic Respondents, Cross-Scale Media Brokers, Local News Brokers, and Peripheral Generalists. The findings show that local-oriented online communities function as local information infrastructures which depend on uneven but complementary forms of resident participation.

articles.title: Multiracial young adults’ experiences of Whiteness as a wage and tax
articles.abstract: Debates persist on the racial position of multiracial Americans, namely whether this population will “become White” or not. However, the premise of this question is predicated on a monoracial paradigm of race that cannot fully account for the experiences of multiracial individuals. Multiracial experiences with Whiteness, including ways they conform to and confound monoracial expectations, have the potential to reshape our understandings of racial constructions, boundaries, and futures, particularly considering shifting racial demographics. One necessary precursor toward these insights lies in the distinctions between how multiracial and monoracial individuals experience Whiteness. Drawing on thirty-seven in-depth interviews with multiracial young adults with White ancestry in the Midwest, I argue that multiracial individuals experience Whiteness as a wage (privileges) and a tax (costs). Like monoracial Whites, multiracial individuals viewed as White can receive public and psychological wages, yet these wages are offset by an inseparable “racial tax,” which is predicated on the contingent and exclusive nature of Whiteness. These results underscore the utility of calling attention to the monoracial structure, as well as recognizing and theorizing beyond its limits.

articles.title: ThSQCA: Reproducible Threshold-Sweep Workflows for QCA in R
articles.abstract: Qualitative Comparative Analysis (QCA) sets thresholds when constructing sets from continuous scales. A standard analysis, however, is fixed to a single set of thresholds, so it does not directly reveal how the sufficiency structure changes across different outcome levels. Researchers can repeat the analysis at individual thresholds, but comparing the emergence and disappearance of configurations, solution fit, and the presence of multiple minimal solutions while keeping settings consistent requires additional implementation. This article introduces the R package Threshold-Sweep Qualitative Comparative Analysis (ThSQCA), which addresses this gap. ThSQCA uses the QCA package as its computational engine and provides a common workflow to run, aggregate, visualize, and report analyses that systematically vary the outcome threshold, the condition thresholds, or both. In a consumer survey of usage intention toward Starbucks (n = 336), moderate target levels of usage intention yielded multiple sufficient paths, whereas the highest target level left only one narrow path, with solution coverage dropping substantially. Varying the threshold that defines service delivery as high further produced different sufficiency structures, including cases with no solution, for the same high level of usage intention. Such differences cannot be observed in a single-threshold analysis. ThSQCA does not automatically select the correct threshold. It is a diagnostic and comparative workflow that clarifies, over a research- or practice-relevant range, at which levels a conclusion holds and where it changes. This allows QCA results to be evaluated not as an answer specific to one threshold, but as decision-relevant information that depends on the target level.

articles.title: What the Balkan Barometer Can and Cannot Rank: A Measurement Audit of the Western Balkans' Flagship Survey
articles.abstract: The Balkan Barometer, annual since 2015 with roughly 1,000 face-to-face interviews in each of six Western Balkan economies, is cited across the region as what its citizens think. We evaluate it as a measuring instrument from the Regional Cooperation Council's own released microdata for 2023 to 2025, within a total survey error frame. The published percentages reproduce from the microdata (440 of 444 cells within one point). Of the fifteen pairwise economy differences on each of thirty 2025 headline items, 71 percent are resolvable at a design effect of 2.0, but only 40 percent of adjacent-rank pairs are: six points is the least difference at which two economies of 1,000 can be told apart. The WB6 figure is an unweighted mean of six economies whose populations differ tenfold; under population weights it moves by 6 to 12 points on the most-quoted items, including EU membership (64 versus 58 percent in 2025). Of twenty-three headline series present in all three editions, four are comparable throughout; between 2024 and 2025 the changed series moved by 14 points on average against 6 for the stable ones. The 2025 institutional battery is scalar invariant once two cells are freed, police in Kosovo* and courts in North Macedonia; with them freed, Kosovo*'s raw-score lead disappears and the top three economies cannot be separated. The two published editions score 16 of 32 on a documentation checklist built from what the ESS, the Eurobarometer and the AAPOR Transparency Initiative publish routinely; precision, comparability and limitations score zero. We report two database errors and a file anomaly for correction, and close with the four things a technical report would need to contain.

articles.title: Different spaces, different citizens? Explaining online and offline volunteering and citizenship behavior through the Civic Voluntarism Model
articles.authors: Arjen de Wit, Marlou Ramaekers, Stephanie Koolen-Maas, Rene Bekkers
articles.abstract: Online ways of communication have radically changed the face of volunteerism, often described as ‘virtual volunteering’, ‘online volunteering’ or ‘digital volunteering’. In this paper we examine if those individuals engaged in online spaces, both in formal organizations and in self-organized communities, are different from those engaged in offline (in-person) volunteering. To understand how the four distinct types of voluntary participation (offline volunteers, online volunteers, offline self-organized citizens, online self-organized citizens) attract the same or different individuals, we anchor our analysis in the Civic Voluntarism Model (CVM). Using panel survey data from the Netherlands, we find that offline and online volunteers show higher engagement and especially networks, and this also holds for people who participate as citizens in their neighborhood. ‘Being asked’ to volunteer is the strongest correlate of volunteering, both offline and online, as well as offline citizenship. Recruitment networks are less important for online participation. Strikingly, online self-organized platforms are able to reach new groups of citizens that are not stratified by similar prerequisites for participation. These findings provide valuable insights for volunteer managers, activists, and policy makers who use online channels to recruit and retain volunteers.

articles.title: What Affective Polarization Is Made Of: Components, Targets, Cleavages and Emotions in Five Multiparty Democracies
articles.authors: Mabelle Kretchner, Bendegúz Plesz, Eran Halperin, Julia Elad-Strenger, Sivan hirsch hoefler, Adva Gruenwald, Zsolt Boda
articles.abstract: The more affective polarization (AP) is studied, the clearer it becomes that a single score conceals what it is made of. The score has two sides, ingroup attachment and outgroup hostility, and the two need not be balanced. AP runs toward different targets, it runs along a different divide in each system, and the affect itself is made of distinct emotions. Comparative work has taken up each of these layers, but in the studies we are aware of, never all together, so what any given score is made of is still not known: two democracies with similar AP levels may be facing quite different things. Drawing on preregistered survey data from five multiparty democracies (Germany, Hungary, Italy, Poland, Israel; N = 5,151), we map all four layers in one design: AP and its two sides toward parties, voters, and ideological blocs; where attachment and hostility sit across the parties of each system; and the associations of six discrete emotions with AP. In all countries, AP drew more on ingroup attachment than on outgroup hostility, and disappointment and anger rather than hatred were associated with AP toward parties and voters. What differed was where the affect settled: which parties concentrated it, and whether the ideological bloc carried it at all. Hatred appeared only at the bloc level and only in some systems, at the target whose scores were otherwise among the lowest. We discuss the importance of unfolding these layers together in comparative research, for a better understanding of AP and for addressing it.

articles.title: Evaluating the discrepancies in funding metadata across bibliographic and administrative databases: the case of South Korea’s public research funding
articles.abstract: Funding metadata underpins the identification of the relationship between research funding and outputs, yet its coverage and accuracy vary across databases. I examine discrepancies in funding metadata for South Korean government-funded research by comparing records from South Korea’s National Science & Technology Information Service (NTIS) with Web of Science and OpenAlex. Linking NTIS-reported publications across these three sources reveals substantial divergence: few project identifiers and publication-project pairs were captured across all three databases. These discrepancies stem from multiple compounding factors, including incomplete database indexing, optional or inconsistent funder acknowledgement policies, and variations in how project identifiers are described and extracted. Accounting for identifier variations and multi-phase project structures recovers additional matches but does not substantially close the overall gap. A logistic regression model further demonstrates that whether funding sources are acknowledged is linked to structural factors, such as stakeholder complexity regarding the co-authors and institutions involved in a publication. This indicates that acknowledgement omissions are driven not merely by technical limitations in metadata collection, but also by institutional constraints surrounding research funding. Furthermore, acknowledgement lag patterns, where the time gap between project execution and publication active years is virtually zero, point to systemic weaknesses in administrative reporting workflows. The paper concludes by recommending policy actions for funding agencies to ensure the interoperability and reliability of NTIS records. These findings underscore the need to evaluate funding metadata discrepancies not merely as a technical indexing challenge, but as an issue deeply embedded within the institutional structures of research systems.

articles.title: Between Finality and Accuracy: Vote Recount Institutions in European Democracies
articles.abstract: Vote recounts sit at the intersection of vote counting, dispute resolution, and post-electoral procedure, yet comparative knowledge of how democracies actually conduct them remains scarce. Drawing on a structured, focused comparison across ten European democracies that operate single-instance electoral judiciaries, we examine the institutional settings within which recounts take place. We frame the observed variation through what we term the finality-accuracy dilemma, the tension between treating certified results as settled and ensuring that declared results faithfully reflect voter preferences. Five dimensions structure our analysis, namely standing, threshold conditions, decision-making body, scope, and procedural deadlines. We identify five recurring configurations and find that decision-making body type aligns systematically with position on the finality-accuracy spectrum, with judicial bodies clustering on the finality side and parliamentary bodies adopting accuracy-leaning flexibility. No sampled system employs automatic margin-based triggers, and ordered recounts were partial rather than comprehensive in scope.

articles.title: Resilience in a Hybrid Security Culture: Georgia between Institutional Continuity and Political Realignment
articles.abstract: Challenging the common understanding in the relevant literature, this study reconceptualizes resilience to hybrid threats as a politically mediated process rather than purely a matter of institutional capacity-building. To examine how policy frameworks and political rhetoric interact to shape resilience, it traces Georgia’s security culture in the aftermath of the Russo-Georgian war. Through intertextual discourse analysis, the article cross-examines the institutional architecture of digital resilience, encompassing cybersecurity (systemic), media regulation (protective) and media literacy (empowerment) measures, with the government’s shifting rhetoric (2023–2025), while interview data provide contextual insights. The analysis reveals a hybrid security culture manifested in fragmented governance and discursive struggle over resilience. Although formal policy frameworks normatively align with the West and consistently identify Russia as the principal security threat, governmental rhetoric portrays the same Western actors as sources of foreign interference and prioritizes political autonomy over cooperation while still invoking commitments to the constitutionally enshrined Euro-Atlantic trajectory. This dichotomy between institutional design and political discourse results in strategic ambiguity. It suggests that in hybrid regimes formal frameworks may function symbolically to signal external alignment, while practice is determined by short-term political calculations and discretionary authority, leaving institutions and societies vulnerable to evolving forms of foreign interference.
